questions.question_text: What are the endpoint, domain, and range of $y = \sqrt{x - 8} + 10$?

options.why: Read the horizontal shift straight off the sign printed in $x - 8$, taking $h = -8$ and shifting left instead of right.
Treated the $+10$ outside the root as a downward shift, taking $k = -10$.
Reversed both shifts at once, reading $y = \sqrt{x - 8} + 10$ as a move left $8$ and down $10$.

questions.solution_text:
Set $x - 8 = 0 \implies x = 8$, so endpoint is $(8, 10)$.
Domain: $[8, \infty)$
Range: $[10, \infty)$

questions.question_text: What are the domain and range of the reflected square root function $y = -\sqrt{x + 4} + 1$?

options.why: Ignored the negative sign in front of the radical which reflects the range downwards.
Reflected the domain to the left instead of keeping $x \ge -4$.
Used $x \ge 4$ instead of solving $x + 4 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -4$.

questions.solution_text:
$x + 4 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -4$, so Domain is $[-4, \infty)$.
The negative sign before the root gives $y \le 1$, so Range is $(-\infty, 1]$.

options.why: Has domain $[3, \infty)$ (opens to the right) instead of $(-\infty, 3]$.
Has range $(-\infty, -4]$ (opens downwards) instead of $[-4, \infty)$.
Has vertical shift $+4$ (endpoint at $(3, 4)$) instead of $-4$.

questions.solution_text:
Endpoint: $(3, -4)$
Domain from graph: $(-\infty, 3] \implies y = \sqrt{3 - x} + k$
Vertical shift $k = -4 \implies y = \sqrt{3 - x} - 4$
Range: $[-4, \infty)$

questions.question_text: Which table of values correctly plots integer points on the curve $y = \sqrt{x + 1} - 3$?

options.why: Took $h = +1$ from $x + 1$, starting the table at $x = 1$ and shifting the curve right instead of left.
Reversed the vertical shift, evaluating $\sqrt{x + 1} + 3$ instead of $\sqrt{x + 1} - 3$.
Reversed both shifts, evaluating $\sqrt{x - 1} + 3$ so the curve moves right $1$ and up $3$.

questions.question_text: What are the endpoint and range of $y = 3 - \sqrt{x - 2}$?

options.why: Missed the minus sign before the root, which forces $y \le 3$.
Reversed the sign of $h = 2$.
Treated the constant $3$ as negative.

questions.solution_text:
Rewrite as $y = -\sqrt{x - 2} + 3$.
Endpoint is $(2, 3)$.
Since the square root is subtracted, range is $y \le 3$ or $(-\infty, 3]$.

questions.question_text: What are the endpoint, domain, and range of $y = \sqrt{x + 7}$?

options.why: Used $x \ge 7$ instead of solving $x + 7 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -7$.
Treated the horizontal shift $+7$ as a vertical shift.
Flipped the domain inequality to $x \le -7$.

questions.solution_text:
Set $x + 7 = 0 \implies x = -7$, so endpoint is $(-7, 0)$.
Domain: $[-7, \infty)$
Range: $[0, \infty)$

questions.question_text: What are the endpoint, domain, and range of $y = \sqrt{x - 2} + 5$?

options.why: Read $x-2$ as a shift left $2$ instead of solving $x-2=0$.
Treated $+5$ outside the root as a shift down $5$.
Reversed the domain inequality, using $x\le2$ instead of $x-2\ge0$.

questions.solution_text:
Set $x-2=0 \implies x=2$, so the endpoint is $(2,5)$.
Domain: $[2,\infty)$.
Since $\sqrt{x-2}\ge0$, $y\ge5$.
Range: $[5,\infty)$.

questions.solution_text:
Translate $y = \sqrt{x}$ left $5$ units and down $1$ unit.
The endpoint moves from $(0,0)$ to $(-5,-1)$.
At $x=-4$, $y=\sqrt{1}-1=0$; at $x=-1$, $y=\sqrt{4}-1=1$; at $x=4$, $y=\sqrt{9}-1=2$.
The curve starts at $(-5,-1)$ and increases to the right through $(-4,0)$, $(-1,1)$ and $(4,2)$, with a decreasing gradient.
Therefore Sketch A is correct.

Used the plotted $y$-coordinate $4$ as the dilation factor without dividing by the original height $f(4)=2$.
Reversed the height ratio, calculating $f(4)\div g(4)=2\div4=\frac{1}{2}$ instead of $g(4)\div f(4)$.

questions.solution_text:
At $x=4$, $f(4)=\sqrt{4}=2$, while the graph shows $g(4)=4$.
The vertical dilation factor is $4\div2=2$.
At $x=9$, $2\sqrt{9}=6$, matching the other labelled point.
Therefore $g(x)=2\sqrt{x}$.
